doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Carol Burnett Show stories: stolen props, Jonathan Winters, Tim Conway
summary: Two bandmates stole set items and a giant pepper mill, and a candelabra went missing at Carol Burnett's Christmas party with Basie's band. Winters entertained the band and Conway broke up Harvey Korman.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Can you recall any memorable moments in all those live T.V. shows that stick out for you?

Oh there was, when we were doing the Carol Burnett Show, it was done at CBS, which is down at — well you don’t know the city but it’s down on Fairfax and Beverly which is down in West Los Angeles sort of, near Beverly Hills. And they had some soap operas that were done there also. And they had these sets that were set up permanently, like a drawing room, that they would re-use and they would leave them set up permanently. And they were fully, I guess you’d say decorated, with things on the tables and © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

everything. And there were a couple of guys that used to go shopping on the breaks that were in the band, and they’d steal things. And these same, this same two people, there was a restaurant we used to eat at on our breaks that we’d go to and they had these huge pepper mills. They were about three feet tall I guess, or four maybe. I mean the waiter would have to stand back from the table to make it to the salad or whatever he’s putting it on. Well they stole one of those, put it under their jacket and just walked out with it. And then Carol Burnett would have wonderful Christmas parties. She’d have them at the Los Angeles Yacht Club. And she’d hire name bands. We had Basie’s band one time, this was for the cast and crew of the show. And wonderful buffets, you couldn’t ask for better. And there was this huge silver candelabra that somebody stole. And I never found out for sure but we always suspected it might have been our same kleptos.
Oh gee, I’ve heard of some bad habits of musicians, but not that one.

Well I mean, and these people were well to do. I mean as far as musicians go, they did well. And it wasn’t the money, it was the adventure I guess. That’s strange. You know I’m sure there are many — like for instance, I can’t give you specific instances, but on the Carol Burnett Show, Jonathan Winters was a frequent guest there and he was just sensational. And he used to always love to come over to the band area and entertain the band, which he would do. And that was always fun. And that show was with Tim Conway, and Harvey Korman, that was as much fun as I ever had watching those guys work. Tim Conway would just completely destroy Harvey Korman. Harvey Korman could not continue, you know, he was just breaking up so much. It was a lot of fun. That made the work a lot of fun.
I can’t imagine how you guys would keep playing without laughing.
